review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how it uses simp. I found nothing that justifies a finding under the simp-interface rubric. The file declares no @[simp] lemmas and no simp-set attributes. `expMulMulExp` is a private-style helper that is unfolded by name (`unfold`, `simp [expMulMulExp]`) only within this file; a grep found all 12 of its occurrences here. Adding simp lemmas for it would be speculative. The public lemmas `SemiconjBy.star_right`, `IsStarNormal.commute_star_right` and the `Set.Pairwise` lemmas have hypotheses that simp could not discharge. Those hypotheses are normality and commutation, and `Commute.star_right` in Algebra/Star/Basic.lean is likewise not simp. So they are correctly left as plain lemmas. Within proofs, the `simp only [smul_neg, even_two, Even.neg_pow, neg_smul]` calls and the simp-set arguments look targeted, and I saw no sign of competing rules or rewrite cycles. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out simp behaviour that only shows up when compiling.
